title: Multi-File Substrate Mutation — Cross-File Graph Self-Modification
key_findings: An agent executing in File A modifies File B's contents in place (creates a RESULT node, supersedes a node, redirects an edge) — the fourth flavor of self-modification, cross-file in-place mutation.
Both files commit atomically or neither does: an injected mid-transaction failure leaves both files byte-identical (WAL rollback), with no dangling edge and no partial node.
The substrate boundary is discovered by following cross-file edges transitively (3 files, A->B->C), with no manifest or registry.
A cross-file mutation is immediately live for traversal across the file boundary — no parse/compile/deploy step (structural liveness).
Demonstrated for 2-3 files; the WAL primitive is N-file-shaped but unbounded-N is not proven here (that is the CIP spec's burden).
